So the kit's own review, criterion and run rows ship into each adopter's docs/agents/*.jsonl, and so does its run history (kit file names, findings, model names). The adopter's proof audit then counts correction rows that are not its own — evidence: harness.conf sets HARNESS_AGENT_DIR="running-files/agents"; init.sh:56 runs `cp -R running-files/. docs/` and nothing in init.sh truncates *.jsonl (grep "jsonl" in init.sh finds nothing); check-the-work.sh:849 `verify` FAILS a branch that adds no row to that log, so the kit has to commit a real row there to pass its own step. The templates are empty today (0 bytes), but the next judged kit commit fills them — fix: point the kit's HARNESS_AGENT_DIR at a folder that is not shipped (e.g. a kit-only `agent-logs/`, or a path under the ignored HARNESS_LOG_DIR), and keep running-files/agents/*.jsonl empty; or have init.sh empty docs/agents/*.jsonl after the copy and add an init-test row that asserts it.

Same-family review (local red-team agent).
VERDICT: FINDINGS
GOAL: CANNOT TELL — the delta does what its summary says (default_base reaches scan/answer/verify; run_hooks passes CTW_BASE; the empty-`--base` row holds), but the PROOF lines ("scripts/run-all-gates.sh --full" verdict, selftest.sh and init-test.sh summaries, the leak grep) are not in the material; only the two matrix lines the sub-session quoted are.
F1 [P3] [important] scripts/check-the-work.d/10-success-criterion.sh:419 — default_base does not end the way check-the-work.sh resolve_base does, although its comment (line 407: "the same order as check-the-work.sh resolve_base") says it does. When HARNESS_BASE_REF is set but neither it nor its local part is a commit, the hook quietly falls back to `main`; the driver uses the configured ref and stops with an error naming it (check-the-work.sh:223 `base="$want"   # merge_base names it in its error`). So a by-hand `scan`/`answer`/`verify` silently scans against the wrong base — evidence, reproduced in a scratch repo (branch main, feature branch, harness.conf `HARNESS_BASE_REF="origin/develop"`, no develop): `10-success-criterion.sh scan` printed a full FLAG against main with nothing on stderr about the base, while `check-the-work.sh verify --branch feat` stopped with "no merge base between 'origin/develop' and 'feat'"; `10-success-criterion.sh verify` (CTW_BRANCH=feat) reported "verify FAIL ... step was skipped" against main — fix: in default_base, after the loop, `printf '%s' "$want"` when HARNESS_BASE_REF is set (keep `main` only when it is unset), and print the derived base on stderr as resolve_base does; add one row (HARNESS_BASE_REF names a ref that does not exist while main exists -> exit 3 naming that ref).
F2 [P3] [important] running-files/agents/README.md:5 (with harness.conf:28-30) — the round-1 F1 fix states "the kit logs its own reviews elsewhere, so no row ships to a new project", but a new project is made by running scripts/init.sh IN a fresh clone of the kit (init.sh:2 "turn a fresh clone of this boilerplate into a working project skeleton"; it `cd "$ROOT"` and works in place). `.harness/agents/criterion.jsonl` and `.harness/agents/reviews.jsonl` are TRACKED (git ls-files .harness: both listed, one row each, added in 92d3553), init.sh removes only `.harness/baselines` (init.sh:202 `rm -rf .harness/baselines`) and its prune list names neither file — so the kit's own review and criterion rows still ship into every new project, just under .harness/ instead of docs/. Inert there (the new harness.conf leaves HARNESS_AGENT_DIR at docs/agents), but the claim is false and the leak is not closed — fix: have init.sh empty or remove `.harness/agents/*.jsonl` (or add them to the printed `git rm` list) and prove it in init-test.sh; or reword the README claim to what is true.
F3 [P3] [nit] scripts/check-the-work.sh:92-93 and scripts/check-the-work.d/10-success-criterion.sh:35,38 — the hook-point contract lists the hook env as CTW_STAGE, CTW_ROOT, CTW_STATE, CTW_BRANCH, CTW_LOG, CTW_JUDGEMENT and now omits CTW_BASE, which run_hooks passes since this change (check-the-work.sh:183; empty at judge, the resolved base at verify); line 35 also gives the verify default as "CTW_BASE, then HARNESS_BASE_REF", skipping CHECK_THE_WORK_BASE that default_base reads second — fix: add "CTW_BASE (the base ref this step resolved; empty at judge)" to both env lists and say "CTW_BASE, CHECK_THE_WORK_BASE, then HARNESS_BASE_REF" on line 35.
UNSEEN: the PROOF outputs (run-all-gates --full, selftest.sh, init-test.sh, the leak grep) — not in the prompt and not run by me; the NOT SHOWN files of the prompt (check-the-work.sh body beyond run_hooks/resolve_base/verify/judge, review_tally.py, log-agent-run.py, refs-index.py, resume-brief.sh, second-opinion.sh, session-state.sh and the test matrices other than the two delta files) were not reviewed beyond targeted greps; I ran scripts/ctw-success-criterion-test.sh myself on the current work tree: "ctw-success-criterion matrix: 116 pass, 0 fail, 0 known-defect (open findings)" (matches the claim); I did not run check-the-work-test.sh (its 229-row claim is unchecked by me). ASSUMPTION (not a finding): the delta moves the verify hook from the LOCAL `main` to `origin/main` first (via the driver's CTW_BASE and default_base); when the lead has merged branches locally and not pushed, the merge base with the remote ref is older, so a later branch's scan can include other branches' commits and flag them — this now matches judge (which already used the driver's origin-first stored base) and the driver's own resolve_base, so it is consistent, but whether "remote ref first" is the intended base for a lead who merges before pushing is not recorded anywhere I found (grep of ci/, running-files/, dot-claude/, the READMEs for HARNESS_BASE_REF: one unrelated hit).
